s:
Match List-I (Satellite) with List-II (Launch vehicle):
List-I (Satellite) | List-II (Launch vehicle)
a. DS-SAR | i. PSLV-C56
b. Aditya-L1 | ii. GSLV-F15
c. RISAT-2BR1 | iii. PSLV-C48
d. NVS-02 | iv. PSLV-C57
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: DS-SAR (Singapore radar satellite) – PSLV-C56, July 2023; Aditya-L1 – PSLV-C57, Sep 2023; RISAT-2BR1 – PSLV-C48, Dec 2019; NVS-02 (NavIC) – GSLV-F15, Jan 2025.

s:
Consider the following statements about recent ISRO launches:
1. RISAT-1, launched by PSLV-C19 in 2012, carries an X-band Synthetic Aperture Radar.
2. EOS-07 was launched by SSLV-D2 on 10 February 2023.
3. EOS-08, launched by SSLV-D3 in August 2024, was the last development flight of the SSLV.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: RISAT-1 (PSLV-C19, 2012) carries a C-band SAR for day-night, all-weather imaging; X-band radar is on RISAT-2BR1.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. INSAT-3DS, a meteorological satellite launched by GSLV-F14, was funded by the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
2. NVS-02, a NavIC satellite launched by GSLV-F15 in January 2025, missed its intended orbit.
3. NISAR, the Earth observation mission with NASA, was launched by GSLV-F17 in July 2025.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: NISAR flew on GSLV-F16 on 30 July 2025; GSLV-F17 launched EOS-05 (4 Sep 2026).

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The SpaDeX mission is a key step towards the Bharatiya Antariksh Station.
Reason (R): Building and servicing a space station needs docking, which SpaDeX demonstrated when its two spacecraft docked on 16 January 2025.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: docking capability is needed for the Bharatiya Antariksh Station (and Chandrayaan-4); SpaDeX (PSLV-C60) docked on 16 Jan 2025.

s:
Consider the following statements about records of Indian launch vehicles:
1. BlueBird Block-2 (about 6,100 kg), a direct-to-smartphone broadband satellite launched by LVM3-M6, is the heaviest payload launched by an Indian rocket.
2. The first dedicated commercial flight of the LVM3 carried 36 OneWeb satellites in 2022.
3. Kalpana-1, India's first exclusive weather satellite, was launched by the GSLV in 2002.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Kalpana-1 (2002) was launched by the PSLV.

s:
Match List-I (Satellite) with List-II (Builder):
List-I (Satellite) | List-II (Builder)
a. ANUSAT | i. IIT Kanpur
b. Jugnu | ii. NMIT Bengaluru
c. STUDSAT-2 | iii. Anna University
d. WeSAT | iv. LBS Institute of Technology for Women
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: ANUSAT (2009) – Anna University, the first student satellite launched by ISRO; Jugnu (PSLV-C18, 2011) – IIT Kanpur; STUDSAT-2 – NMIT Bengaluru; WeSAT (on POEM-3) – LBS Institute of Technology for Women.

s:
Match List-I (Satellite launched by ISRO) with List-II (Country / agency):
List-I (Satellite) | List-II (Country / agency)
a. KITSAT-3 | i. Italy
b. AGILE | ii. European Space Agency
c. NovaSAR | iii. South Korea
d. Proba-3 | iv. United Kingdom
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: KITSAT-3 – South Korea (PSLV-C2, 1999); AGILE – Italy, gamma-ray astronomy (PSLV-C8, 2007); NovaSAR – UK (PSLV-C42, 2018); Proba-3 – ESA (PSLV-C59, Dec 2024).

s:
Consider the following statements about ISRO's foreign customer launches:
1. ISRO has launched 433 foreign satellites of more than 34 countries.
2. More than half of these foreign satellites belong to the United Kingdom.
3. ISRO launched 72 OneWeb satellites in two LVM3 missions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: over half of the 433 foreign satellites are from the United States; OneWeb (UK) supplied the 72 satellites flown on two LVM3 missions.

s:
Consider the following statements about private Indian satellites:
1. TSAT-1A, a sub-metre optical satellite, was built by Tata Advanced Systems with Satellogic at Vemagal in Karnataka.
2. Pixxel's hyperspectral satellite Shakuntala (TD-2) was India's first private commercial imaging satellite.
3. Both TSAT-1A and Shakuntala were launched by ISRO's PSLV.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: both TSAT-1A (Apr 2024) and Shakuntala (Apr 2022) were launched on SpaceX's Falcon 9.

s:
Match List-I (Failed mission) with List-II (Payload lost):
List-I (Mission) | List-II (Payload lost)
a. GSLV-F02 (2006) | i. EOS-02 and AzaadiSAT
b. GSLV-F10 (2021) | ii. EOS-09
c. SSLV-D1 (2022) | iii. EOS-03
d. PSLV-C61 (2025) | iv. INSAT-4C
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: GSLV-F02 lost INSAT-4C; GSLV-F10 lost EOS-03 (cryogenic stage); SSLV-D1 put EOS-02 and AzaadiSAT in a wrong orbit; PSLV-C61 (18 May 2025) lost EOS-09 (third stage).

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The PSLV-C62 mission of 12 January 2026 failed because its first stage did not ignite.
Reason (R): PSLV-C62 lost EOS-N1 'Anvesha' along with 15 co-passenger satellites.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is false: the failure was a roll-rate disturbance at the end of the third stage, not first-stage non-ignition. R is true: EOS-N1 'Anvesha' and 15 co-passengers were lost.

s:
Match List-I (Experiment) with List-II (Launch vehicle, year):
List-I (Experiment) | List-II (Vehicle, year)
a. SRE-1 (Space Capsule Recovery Experiment) | i. PSLV-C58, 2024
b. CARE (crew module re-entry) | ii. PSLV-C53, 2022
c. POEM | iii. PSLV-C7, 2007
d. POEM-3 | iv. LVM3, 2014
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: SRE-1 – PSLV-C7 (2007); CARE – LVM3 (2014); POEM – PSLV-C53 (2022); POEM-3 – PSLV-C58 (2024) (POEM-2 was on C55, 2023).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The PSLV Orbital Experimental Module (POEM) uses the spent PS4 stage as an orbital laboratory.
2. TRISHNA, a thermal infrared mission to measure land surface temperature and water stress, is a joint mission of ISRO and JAXA.
3. Proba-3 uses formation flying of two spacecraft to create an artificial solar eclipse for studying the corona.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: ISRO's partner in TRISHNA is CNES (France), not JAXA.

s:
Match List-I (Satellite) with List-II (Application):
List-I (Satellite) | List-II (Application)
a. EMISAT | i. Ocean studies
b. Oceansat | ii. Electronic intelligence
c. NVS series | iii. Science (X-ray polarimetry)
d. XPoSat | iv. Navigation (NavIC)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: EMISAT – electronic intelligence (strategic); Oceansat – ocean; NVS – NavIC navigation; XPoSat – science, with Aditya-L1.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The James Webb Space Telescope, launched on 25 December 2021, is a joint mission of NASA, ESA and CSA.
2. The James Webb Space Telescope observes mainly in the X-ray part of the spectrum.
3. With XPoSat, India became the second country, after NASA's IXPE, to launch a dedicated X-ray polarimetry satellite.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: JWST is an infrared telescope; X-ray polarimetry is the field of IXPE (NASA, Dec 2021) and XPoSat.

s:
Consider the following statements about Mars missions:
1. NASA's Perseverance rover landed in the Jezero crater in February 2021 along with the Ingenuity helicopter.
2. The rover of ESA's ExoMars mission is named Rosalind Franklin.
3. Beagle-2, the lander carried on ESA's Mars Express in 2003, was built by France.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Beagle-2 was a British-built lander; it was lost on landing and found on the surface in 2015.

s:
Match List-I (Space mission / rocket) with List-II (Country):
List-I (Mission) | List-II (Country)
a. SuperView | i. South Korea
b. Nuri (KSLV-II) | ii. Japan
c. EQUULEUS | iii. Israel and France
d. VENµS | iv. China
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: SuperView – China (commercial Earth observation); Nuri – South Korea's first indigenous launcher (June 2022); EQUULEUS – JAXA's steam-propelled CubeSat; VENµS – Israel-France vegetation and environment satellite (2017).

s:
Match List-I (Chinese lunar mission) with List-II (Achievement):
List-I (Mission) | List-II (Achievement)
a. Chang'e-3 (2013) | i. First soil brought back from the far side of the Moon
b. Chang'e-4 (2019) | ii. China's first lunar sample return
c. Chang'e-5 (2020) | iii. First soft landing on the far side of the Moon
d. Chang'e-6 (2024) | iv. China's first soft landing on the Moon
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Chang'e-3 – China's first soft landing (first by anyone since 1976); Chang'e-4 – first far-side soft landing (rover Yutu-2); Chang'e-5 – first Chinese sample return; Chang'e-6 – first far-side soil (returned 25 Jun 2024).

s:
Consider the following statements about lunar missions:
1. NASA's LCROSS hit a polar crater of the Moon in 2009 to look for water.
2. The lunar module of Apollo 11 that landed on 20 July 1969 was named Columbia.
3. Japan's SLIM made Japan the fifth country to soft-land on the Moon.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Apollo 11 lunar module was Eagle (Columbia was the command module, not in the notes as the lander).

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): India signed the US-led Artemis Accords in 2023.
Reason (R): Under NASA's Artemis programme, Artemis IV (2028) is planned as the first crewed landing, near the lunar south pole.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true (India signed in 2023; Artemis IV is now the first crewed landing after Artemis III became a 2027 low-Earth-orbit test), but the mission plan does not explain why India signed the Accords.

s:
Consider the following statements about Chandrayaan-3:
1. It consisted of a Propulsion Module, the lander Vikram and the rover Pragyan, with no orbiter of its own.
2. Its mission life was one lunar day, about 14 Earth days.
3. Its rover Pragyan weighed about 260 kg.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Pragyan weighed about 26 kg (the lander 1,752 kg including the rover; whole craft 3,900 kg).

s:
Consider the following statements about the landing of Chandrayaan-3:
1. Before India, only the USA, the USSR/Russia and Japan had soft-landed on the Moon.
2. The Vikram lander touched down at Shiv Shakti Point on 23 August 2023.
3. India observes 23 August as National Space Day.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the three earlier soft-landers were the USA, USSR/Russia and China; Japan's SLIM became the fifth after India.

s:
Match List-I (Chandrayaan-3 payload) with List-II (Function):
List-I (Payload) | List-II (Function)
a. ChaSTE | i. Moonquakes (seismic activity)
b. ILSA | ii. Studying the Earth from lunar orbit
c. RAMBHA-LP | iii. Plasma density
d. SHAPE | iv. Surface thermal profile
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: ChaSTE (lander) – thermal profile; ILSA (lander) – moonquakes; RAMBHA-LP (lander) – plasma density; SHAPE (Propulsion Module) – observes Earth from lunar orbit.

s:
Consider the following statements about Chandrayaan-3 payloads:
1. The APXS found the lunar soil to be rich in aluminium.
2. The Laser Retroreflector Array (LRA) on the lander is a passive instrument of NASA.
3. The LIBS on the rover confirmed sulphur on the lunar surface in situ.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: APXS found the soil rich in iron and magnesium and poor in aluminium.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan):
1. It entered Mars orbit on 24 September 2014.
2. It made India the first Asian nation to reach Mars orbit.
3. With it ISRO became the fourth agency to reach Mars, after NASA, Roscosmos and CNSA.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the three earlier agencies were NASA, USSR/Roscosmos and ESA, not China's CNSA.

s:
Consider the following statements about Mangalyaan:
1. It carried seven scientific payloads.
2. The Methane Sensor for Mars was one of its payloads.
3. Designed for six months, it worked for about eight years until contact was lost in 2022.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: MOM carried 5 payloads (Methane Sensor for Mars, Lyman Alpha Photometer, Mars Colour Camera, MENCA, TIS).

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Methane in the Martian atmosphere is cited, with water and gypsum, as evidence for possible life on Mars.
Reason (R): Methane on Mars was first measured by NASA's Spirit rover.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true. R is false: methane on Mars was first measured by ESA's Mars Express (also by NASA's Curiosity), not by Spirit.

s:
Match List-I (Space shuttle) with List-II (Fact):
List-I (Shuttle) | List-II (Fact)
a. Columbia | i. Last shuttle mission, STS-135 (2011)
b. Challenger | ii. First shuttle flight, STS-1 (1981)
c. Discovery | iii. Hubble servicing with six new gyroscopes (Dec 1999)
d. Atlantis | iv. Crew repaired the Solar Maximum Mission (1984)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Columbia flew STS-1 (Apr 1981); Challenger's crew repaired the Solar Maximum Mission (STS-41C, 1984); Discovery serviced Hubble in Dec 1999 (STS-103); Atlantis flew the last mission STS-135 (Jul 2011).

s:
Consider the following statements about Chandrayaan-2:
1. Its Vikram lander crash-landed at Jawahar Point in September 2019.
2. The Union Cabinet approved the mission in 2008.
3. Its orbiter is still working.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: Vikram hard-landed at Tiranga Point; Jawahar Point is the impact site of Chandrayaan-1's Moon Impact Probe.

s:
Consider the following statements about Aditya-L1:
1. It was launched by PSLV-C57 from the Second Launch Pad at Sriharikota.
2. It orbits the Sun-Earth L1 point, about 15 million km from the Earth.
3. It was inserted into its halo orbit on 6 January 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: L1 is about 1.5 million km from the Earth.

s:
Match List-I (Aditya-L1 payload) with List-II (What it studies):
List-I (Payload) | List-II (Studies)
a. VELC | i. Hard X-rays
b. SUIT | ii. Photosphere and chromosphere (near-UV)
c. HEL1OS | iii. Solar corona
d. PAPA | iv. Solar-wind electrons and ions
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: VELC – corona; SUIT – photosphere and chromosphere in near-UV; HEL1OS – hard X-ray (SoLEXS is soft X-ray); PAPA – solar-wind electrons and ions.

s:
Consider the following statements about Aditya-L1 payloads:
1. The VELC was built by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics.
2. The SUIT was built by IUCAA.
3. Aditya-L1 carries seven payloads – four remote-sensing and three in-situ.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: VELC (IIA), SUIT (IUCAA); 7 payloads = 4 remote sensing (VELC, SUIT, SoLEXS, HEL1OS) + 3 in-situ (ASPEX, PAPA, magnetometer).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. AstroSat observes in the X-ray, optical and UV bands simultaneously.
2. UVIT and LAXPC are payloads of AstroSat.
3. The POLIX payload of XPoSat was developed by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: POLIX was developed by the Raman Research Institute, Bengaluru.

s:
Consider the following statements about Chandrayaan-1:
1. It carried 11 scientific instruments, including NASA's Moon Mineralogy Mapper.
2. The Lyman Alpha Photometer was one of its instruments.
3. NASA's Moon Mineralogy Mapper on it detected water molecules on the lunar surface.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Lyman Alpha Photometer flew on Mangalyaan; Chandrayaan-1 carried Mini-SAR, CIXS, TMC, M3 etc.

s:
Consider the following statements about Chandrayaan-1:
1. Its Moon Impact Probe hit the south polar region on 14 November 2008.
2. The impact site is named Shiv Shakti Point.
3. Contact with the spacecraft was lost on 29 August 2009.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the MIP site is Jawahar Point; Shiv Shakti Point is Chandrayaan-3's landing site.

s:
Match List-I (Mission) with List-II (Launch vehicle):
List-I (Mission) | List-II (Vehicle)
a. AstroSat | i. LVM3-M4
b. Chandrayaan-2 | ii. PSLV-C30
c. Chandrayaan-3 | iii. GSLV Mk III-M1
d. SpaDeX | iv. PSLV-C60
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: AstroSat – PSLV-C30 (2015); Chandrayaan-2 – GSLV Mk III-M1 (2019); Chandrayaan-3 – LVM3-M4 (2023); SpaDeX – PSLV-C60 (30 Dec 2024), which made India the 4th country to dock.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A two-body system has five Lagrange points where a small object can stay balanced.
2. A Hohmann transfer is a fuel-saving elliptical transfer between two orbits using two burns.
3. The Mars Orbiter Mission used a Hohmann transfer to reach Mars.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: Lagrange points L1–L5; a Hohmann transfer is an elliptical two-burn transfer, used by MOM after Earth orbit-raising.

s:
Match List-I (Mission) with List-II (Aim):
List-I (Mission) | List-II (Aim)
a. Shukrayaan-1 | i. Mars landing
b. Chandrayaan-4 | ii. Lunar sample return
c. Mangalyaan-2 | iii. Earth – hazards and climate
d. NISAR | iv. Venus orbiter
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Shukrayaan-1 – Venus orbiter; Chandrayaan-4 – lunar sample return from the south polar region (2028); Mangalyaan-2 – Mars landing (~2030); NISAR – NASA-ISRO Earth observation.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Union Cabinet approved the Venus Orbiter Mission in September 2024 at a cost of Rs 1,236 crore.
2. Under Space Vision 2047, the Bharatiya Antariksh Station is to be set up by 2035.
3. Under Space Vision 2047, an Indian is to land on the Moon by 2047.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the target for an Indian on the Moon is 2040.
